tips.text: THINK OUT LOUD during the interview.
Solve a lot of DSA. Start with neetcode.io, then move on to Striver’s A2Z sheet.
Don’t just run behind getting the correct solution—explore the wrong solutions also.
A correct code/approach in the interview does not guarantee your selection, nor does a wrong one deny you. It's all about how well you are able to explain and articulate your thoughts.
Revise your resume and projects thoroughly: Be ready to discuss your contributions, system design choices, and technical decisions.
Stay calm and composed during interviews: Your attitude matters as much as your answers.
Avoid comparing yourself to others on the interview day.
Be humble and helpful to everyone around you.
Take notes during the Pre-Placement Talk.
Be mindful of your grooming and energy: Wear formals, get a good haircut, get enough sleep, and arrive on time.
Don't take failure personally.
Believe. Trust that everything happens in its own time.

tips.text: Stop using Templates at least one month before Placement.
Learn DSU as it is favourite Topic of every PBC.
Never sit Blank in Interview even if you know that your Approach is complete wrong.
Do CP as a lot of Codeforces and Algorithmic Questions were there. If you have not done CP, try to do CP 31 sheet from TLE Eliminators at least till 1500 Rating starting from 1100.
Have Practice of explaining solutions that is more Important than actually Solving the Problem.
Try to do time bound Practice for OA. You can try Virtual Contests on Codeforces and Leetcode.
Make sure to revise standard DSA questions (Striver's SDE sheet Highly Recommended). Star mark the ones which you felt a lot tougher and make notes.
Try to learn some Advanced concept as well as Topics: Binary Lifting, Tries, DP (digit DP and DP with Bitmasking).
Have some good projects on Resume on which you are strong enough to talk on even for hours. Try to solve some real world problem.
Specifically for PhonePe make sure to learn System Design of Any app as this is for sure guaranteed question in HR Round.
Just make sure to give your 100% Best so that you don't have Anything to Regret.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.description: 4 Questions were to be solved in 1 hour 30 mins

questions.text: You are given n people, labeled from 1 to n. There are m existing friendships represented by two arrays A and B, each of size m, where the i-th friendship is between person A[i] and person B[i]. Two people are considered friends if there is a direct or indirect connection between them (i.e., if they belong to the same connected group of friends). Your task is to determine the minimum number of new friendships that must be formed so that every person is connected directly or indirectly—in other words, so that everyone belongs to a single connected group.

You have N employees and are given an array P of size N, where P[i] indicates the number of ladoos the i-th employee receives. If P[i] = 0, it means the ladoos for that employee are yet to be assigned. You are also given two integers M and K: M is the maximum number of ladoos any employee can get. K is the maximum allowed difference in ladoos between adjacent employees. Your task is to determine the number of valid ways to assign ladoos to the unassigned positions such that: Each unassigned position gets a value between 1 and M. The absolute difference between the ladoos of adjacent employees is at most K.

You are given an integer n, an integer k, and an array arr of size n consisting of integers. For each element arr[i], convert it to its binary representation and define its value as: Sum of (bit × position) where position is 1-based from right in the binary representation. You need to find the number of pairs (i, j) such that: value(arr[i]) + value(arr[j]) == k

You are given: Four houses from Harry Potter: Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw, and Slytherin. Two integers: n: number of students, m: maximum number of students allowed in each house. A list of friendships: pairs of integers (a, b) where student a and student b are friends and must be placed in different houses. A strings, where the i-th string contains the allowed houses for the i-th student. Your task is to determine if it is possible to assign every student to exactly one of their preferred houses such that: 1. No pair of friends is placed in the same house 2. No house has more than m students 3. Each student is assigned to one of their preferred houses. Print "possible" if such an assignment exists, otherwise "impossible".

tips.text: Strong DSA skills are essential – PhonePe places heavy emphasis on problem-solving, with this year’s difficulty being higher than usual. Topics like Tries, Binary Lifting were commonly asked.
CP is a bonus, not a requirement – Being comfortable with CP is a big plus as it improves your problem solving skills.
Internship experience adds value – My interview started with questions about my internship. It’s important to clearly explain what you worked on and the impact you had.
Know your resume inside out – Be fully prepared to talk about everything on your resume, including freelance work, projects, and technical contributions.
Hackathon projects stand out – Projects from hackathons show real-world problem-solving and help you pitch confidently in interviews.
Good communication is crucial – Stay vocal, explain your thought process clearly, and engage with the interviewer. Many technically strong candidates were rejected due to weak soft skills.

Be consistent, not rushed – Consistent DSA practice with concept clarity (not rote learning) made a big difference. I would say even 6-8 months of sincere dedication toward DSA can help you clear any OA.

rounds.name: HM - Round
rounds.description: My HM interview was taken by the Engineering Manager at PhonePe. He started off by asking for my introduction and then started questioning me based on my resume.

questions.text: How would you design instagram stories?

tips.text: My advice would be to not waste time on a question if it doesn’t click, solve others and come back later.
In both of these rounds I made sure to communicate my thought process with the interviewer which is essential for them to understand how you approach a problem.
The key is to brush up your system design knowledge, both in general and PhonePe in specific, and be honest and expressive with your answers.

Solve a wide range of problems and emphasize on concepts like binary search, dp, graphs, dsu, tries and a few niche concepts like binary lifting afterwards. Give contests regularly without any hesitation, it’s better to underperform there than to do it in your interviews. Read editorials rather than asking llms for solutions. A good way to learn is by solving striver’s sheet and then giving contests on any platform of your choice, then practicing pyqs of companies when placements are close.
Know your resume well and research the company you’re interviewing for on a basic level at least.

Learn system design concepts and real world case studies. Also learn fundamentals like dbms, oops and os; they might not be directly asked all the time but will improve your understanding of development and sys design.

rounds.name: OA ( Coding Round)
rounds.description: 90 minutes, 4 Questions, 100 points each (Total 400 points). Platform: DoSelect.

questions.text: There are some n friends and needed to find components.

You are given an array of length n representing the number of laddoos distributed to n people standing in a line. Each person must receive at least 1 and at most m laddoos. Some people have already been assigned laddoos (represented as numbers between 1 and m), while others are yet to be assigned and are marked with a 0 in the array. Your task is to assign laddoos to the unassigned positions such that the final array satisfies the condition: for every pair of adjacent people, the absolute difference between the number of laddoos they receive is less than or equal to k. You need to determine the total number of valid ways to make these assignments such that all constraints are satisfied.
Given an Array of n elements have to find 2 elements whose sum is equal to m and the bit addition is <=k.

Sorting Hat : You are given n students and m, the maximum number of students allowed per house. There are four houses: Slytherin, Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, and Ravenclaw. Each student has a list of preferred houses they can be assigned to. Additionally, some pairs of students are friends and must be placed in different houses. Assign each student to one of their preferred houses such that no house exceeds capacity m and no friends share the same house. Determine if such an assignment is possible.

tips.text: When the number of friend relations is not specified in the input, using Scanner in Java is not ideal, as it relies on knowing how many inputs to read. In such cases, BufferedReader is preferred since it allows reading input line by line until the end.

Don’t waste time on 1 question first try the questions which are able to solve and even if able to solve partially some question its ok, Partial Marking does helps so try to increase the number of total testcases passed across all problems.
For OA prepare all the topics. Should know all the common patterns and able to solve LeetCode medium- hard problems.
Can follow Striver’s series but I also recommend to do blind 75 questions for clearing up basics before proceeding to the advance topics.
Stay calm and confident during Interview. Think out loud during the technical interviews. Even while coding it out keep on explaining and discussing the approach.
Interviewers are helpful in case if not able to proceed they can give hints, after hints try to think on them as they give idea about how to proceed to a particular problem.

Doing CP (Competitive Programming) is highly recommended as this year CP topics were asked. Participating in contests on platforms like Codeforces can significantly enhance your problem-solving skills and help you get accustomed to the pressure of live contests.
